notes: The MKR Motor Carrier is not in the provided catalogue, so a new part type was drafted. Its ports are simplified: the MKR header sockets used in the tutorial (D11/D12 for I2C, D6 for the interrupt, 5V, VIN, GND), the battery terminals (VIN, GND) and the motor terminals M1-M4.

The E2 warnings (carrier1:MKR.5V to mkr1:5V, MKR.VIN to mkr1:VIN, MKR.GND to mkr1:GND) are kept on purpose and are not real problems. The tutorial says to mount the MKR board directly on top of the carrier (second image). The board's header pins plug straight into the carrier's female sockets, so no jumper wire exists between them. Each pin pair is a joined and electrical edge, as the spec requires for a pin pushed into a socket.

Change from the previous version: the assumed internal link between the carrier's VIN terminal and MKR.VIN was removed from the carrier's conducts. The tutorial does not say how the carrier powers the board. Only the shared GND is kept as internal.

The battery and the motor are drawn connected straight to the carrier's screw terminals. The images show no separate jumper wires, so none were added. The tutorial says the battery can also go on the male pins next to the terminal block; the terminal block (VIN/GND) was chosen.
The DC motor is optional in the tutorial. It is included because the circuit image shows it on M1+/M1-. Its polarity is assumed.
The micro USB cable plugs into the MKR board. The usb-cable catalogue type has no ports, so the edges leave the ports null.
The power switch on the carrier is set to ON. It is not a separate part.
